title: Maximal strength training improves running economy in distance runners
authors: Storen O, Helgerud J, Stoa EM, Hoff J
population: Well-trained distance runners (9 male, 8 female); 17 randomized to intervention (4 men, 4 women) or control
findings: Intervention: half-squats, 4 sets of 4 repetitions maximum, 3 times per week for 8 weeks, added to normal endurance training.
Significant improvements in 1RM (33.2%), rate of force development (26.0%), running economy at 70% VO2max (5.0%) and time to exhaustion at maximal aerobic speed (21.3%).
No change in VO2max or body weight; the control group showed no changes.
limitations: Very small sample (n=17, 8 in intervention); single lift (half-squat); lab outcomes only, no race performance; frequency of three sessions per week is a single-trial protocol.
implications: Provides a concrete heavy-lifting template for the engine (4 x 4RM, three times weekly in the trial), but the default frequency stays at 2 sessions per week because the larger meta-analyses show no dose moderation.
Supports heavy lifting for women as well as men, without a body-mass penalty.
